To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
N. gonorrhoeae induces the activation of pro-inflammatory cytokines via a stress response pathway involving the small GTPases Rac and Cdc42, PAK, JNK, AP-1 and the cytokine genes.
Ngo induce stress response kinases including PAK, which direct the signal from Rho GTPases to the JNK/AP- 1 pathway, thereby inducing a proinflammatory cytokine response.
Neisseria gonorrhoae induce the activation of the stress response kinase JNK, which is involved in the activation of AP-1 and inflammatory cytokines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the signaling pathway leading to the activation of pro-inflammatory cytokines by N. gonorrhoeae.
the identification of the molecular components of the Ngo-induced stress response pathway leading to activation of the proinflammatory transcription factor AP-1.
the elucidation of the mechanisms by which the pathogenic Ngo strain induces proinflammatory cytokine production via activation of AP-1 and the stress response kinases JNK and MKK4.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ngo activate AP-1 by a stress response pathway involving PAK, Rac1, Cdc42, JNK, and MKK4, which is a novel mechanism in bacterial pathogen–induced cytokine gene transcription.
N. gonorrhoeae induce a complex network of signaling pathways that involve the activation of AP-1 and proinflammatory cytokine genes.
Ngo-induced cytokine activation requires stress response kinases including PAK/Rac/Cdc42, MEKK1, and MKK4, and that JNK and AP1 play a pivotal role in this signaling cascade.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ngo induce stress response kinases, which are involved in the activation of AP-1 and proinflammatory cytokine genes.
Ngo activate the JNK/AP- 1 cascade via PAK, which is dependent on Rac1/Cdc42 and that this pathway is involved in the induction of proinflammatory genes.
Ngo induce a stress response cascade involving PAK, Rho GTPases, and JNK, which in turn activates AP-1 and proinflammatory cytokine genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Ngo-induced activation of AP-1 involves a stress response pathway.
the stress response kinase PAK is a key regulator in the Ngo-mediated induction of AP-1– and cytokine-dependent inflammatory responses.

Ngo induces a cascade of cellular signaling pathways involving the activation of stress response factors, which leads to the transcriptional activation of AP-1–regulated proinflammatory cytokine genes.
